name: WORM MARKET
subcategory: collectible card game with neural components
description: A collectible card game in which physical cards carry embedded neural-ink triggers — when a BCI-equipped player physically holds a card, it delivers a brief sensory impression (a smell, a texture, a flash of color) tied to that card's in-game ability. Non-BCI players play with the cards as standard print collectibles, experiencing a deliberately flattened version of the game. Cards are sold in randomized packs and traded in secondary markets with prices rivaling small Quanta investments.
story_hooks: A card circulating in the secondary market delivers a neural impression that is actually a fragmented memory — someone's real memory, uploaded illegally.
A teenager develops an addiction to specific card sensory triggers, and their family hires someone to trace the supply chain back to its source.
A Worm Market tournament champion is found to have been using a BCI mod that amplified card triggers into genuine predictive advantage — the line between cheating and augmentation is unclear.
